title: Google Images search reproducibly causes tab crash
body: I am using Firefox 115.0b7 compiled from source on Debian GNU/Linux 10 with a fresh profile and no add-ons. Every Google Images search crashes the tab reproducibly: the results appear briefly and are replaced by “Gah. Your tab just crashed.” stderr says the content process exited on signal 11 at process_util_posix.cc:264. I included the corresponding crash-report URL and would like to know what else I can do to diagnose this.

symptoms_visible: Every Google Images results page briefly displays its results and then changes to “Gah. Your tab just crashed.”
When the tab crashes, stderr says that the content process exited on signal 11.
N0.label: N0 reproducible Google Images crash reported

symptoms_visible: Google Images crashes in normal and troubleshooting modes, with fresh profiles and with both Mozilla-provided and locally compiled Firefox builds.
The same page crashes in Firefox 111, 114, 115 and 116 on Debian 10, while I could not reproduce it on a near-identical Debian 11 machine.
N1.label: N1 browser-version and operating-system scope established

symptoms_visible: The standalone browser test also crashes its tab on an affected older Linux system.
Google Images continues to crash regardless of profile, add-ons, safe mode or Firefox version.
N2.label: N2 standalone reproducer and host details collected

symptoms_visible: The standalone JavaScript test says “ok” in candidate build 1, while candidate build 2 crashes the tab.
N3.label: N3 candidate fix distinguished by paired builds

symptoms_visible: Google Images results and the standalone test open without a tab crash in a Firefox build containing the fix.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on another Linux installation or on a machine with a newer distribution?
Does the crash also happen on a similar machine running a newer Debian release?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens on my Debian 10 machine, but I cannot reproduce it on a near-identical Debian 11 machine. I also tried Ubuntu 18.04.6 in a virtual machine and could not reproduce it there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes on the Debian 10 and Debian 11 machines in exactly the same way, including on a current kernel.
The affected machine is Debian 9 rather than Debian 10, while a similar newer Debian installation is unaffected.

edges.comment: Before engineer engagement, the reporter also volunteered extensive version, safe-mode and debug-stack testing. Reports from additional affected users are folded into the same simulated user side where relevant.

question_patterns: Can you open this standalone browser test and tell me whether the tab crashes or displays “ok”?
Please run the attached JavaScript reproducer that does not depend on Google Images and report the raw result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I opened the standalone test and the tab crashed. It is just a bare script, so there was nothing else rendered before the crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone test displays “ok” and does not crash, even though Google Images still crashes.
The standalone test crashes on Firefox ESR instead of Firefox 114, on the same older Linux system.

question_patterns: What kernel is the affected machine running, and what does ulimit -Ss print?
Please paste uname output and the soft stack limit from the machine where this reproduces.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: One affected Debian Buster machine reports kernel 4.19.0-17-amd64, and the soft stack limit is 8192 KiB.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The affected machine is running kernel 6.1, and the same standalone test crashes there with an 8192 KiB stack limit.

edges.comment: The standalone reproducer was supplied by an engineer and tested by several affected users. Kernel and stack-limit results from affected users are folded into one user side. These are raw measurements; the relationship between the kernel's stack-growth rules and the crash remains engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: Please test both Linux64 candidate builds with the standalone reproducer and report what each one does.
After closing all other Firefox instances, can you compare build 1 and build 2 using the same test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With all other Firefox instances closed, build 1 runs the test and says “ok”; build 2 crashes the tab. Other affected machines produced the same result.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both candidate builds crash the standalone test even after I close every other Firefox instance.
Build 1 says “ok” and build 2 crashes, but I tested with Firefox ESR as my normal installed browser.

edges.comment: Pre-landing paired-build verification. One user initially reported both builds crashing because another Firefox instance was reused, then closed all instances and confirmed the same build-1-good/build-2-bad result as the other testers.

solution.intent: Fix Baseline JIT stack probing on older Linux kernels by using the stack-pointer register while probing large OSR frames, then have the user verify Google Images and the standalone reproducer on a Firefox build containing the landed patch.
solution.concrete_example: Change the Baseline Interpreter OSR stack-probing loop to use RSP while touching the pages of a large frame. This keeps each probe within the distance older x86 Linux kernels permit relative to the current stack pointer. After installing a Firefox build containing the patch, retest both the standalone script and Google Images and report whether either tab still crashes.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers derived the mechanism from crash dumps, disassembly, kernel behavior and the paired builds: Google Images triggered an OSR frame larger than 150 KiB; the existing probe loop touched addresses more than roughly 64 KiB from RSP, so older x86 Linux kernels refused to grow the stack. The reporter supplied crash reports, configuration comparisons, call-stack names and raw test results, but did not independently identify this kernel/JIT interaction. The process_util_posix.cc message is only the parent process observing that the content process died.

edges.comment: Technical resolution: use the stack-pointer register for stack probes. The patch landed with an automated reproducer and was subsequently observed not to crash on affected Debian 9/10 systems in Firefox builds containing the fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: Google Images triggered a Baseline Interpreter OSR frame of more than 150 KiB, and Firefox's stack probes accessed memory too far from RSP for older x86 Linux kernels to extend the stack, causing a segmentation fault.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the cross-version and cross-system evidence, the standalone reproducer, the affected older kernel, and the paired candidate-build result.
The fix must use the stack-pointer register while probing the large JIT stack frame so probes remain within the older kernel's permitted distance from RSP.

Must not treat process_util_posix.cc:264 as the crash cause, blame the reporter's custom build, or propose safe mode, add-on removal, or a fresh profile as the resolution; those directions were contradicted by the collected evidence.
Must ask the user to verify Google Images or the standalone reproducer on a Firefox build containing the landed fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Linux user who compiles Firefox, tests multiple release channels and operating systems, reads native crash stacks, and can run specially provided builds and diagnostic commands.
persona_hint.communication_style: Methodical, precise and proactive; reports exact versions, build IDs, commands and crash URLs, clearly labels tentative conclusions, and promptly performs comparison tests.
